summary.intent: Bundle three pending todos (#5 encrypt share itemName, #8 route shared-folder writes through SDK, #9 remove redundant web folder-seeding) into a single GSD phase, then drive that phase through full automated planning and begin execution while the user is AFK.
summary.outcome: Phase 48 was created with an additional P0 requirement (REQ-1: fix the #498 self-bootstrap regression that is actively redding main's web-e2e), 6 plans across 3 waves were researched, mapped, and verified (0 blockers), all planning artifacts committed to branch `feat/sdk-self-bootstrap-regression-fix-and-shared-folder-metadata`, and Wave 1 execution (48-01, the regression fix) was in flight as the transcript ended.

repo: web-e2e only auto-triggers on push to `main` via `ci-e2e.yml`'s `push: branches: [main]` path — PRs and feature branches get no automatic web-e2e coverage, which is how PR #498's regression slipped through to main.

`web-e2e.yml` already has `workflow_dispatch` with a `ref` input (`ref: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}`), enabling pre-merge branch testing via `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh workflow run web-e2e.yml --ref <branch>` with no CI changes required.
PR #498's self-bootstrap clobbers fresher in-memory folderTree state: `loadFolder` calls unconditional `folderTree.set()` regardless of sequenceNumber, causing the same desync class as PR #489.
The server is zero-knowledge and cannot re-encrypt existing plaintext `itemName` values — legacy rows require lazy client backfill (not a server-side migration UPDATE).
CRDT-IPNS inbox research (#2) would subsume the itemName plaintext leak (#5/M1) but is long-horizon; #5 must be treated as an independent live security finding and not held hostage to #2.

GSD `branching_strategy: phase` creates a new branch off the current HEAD (not origin/main), which can silently rename/replace the user-created branch — requires explicit verification that planning commits were not orphaned.
TypeORM migrations for zero-knowledge schema changes must be additive only (new nullable column, no data UPDATE) to preserve the zero-knowledge invariant.
Shared folders carry a distinct `SharedWriteContext` and can collide on `ipnsName` if merged into `folderTree` — a sibling `sharedFolderTree` keyed by `shareId` is the correct isolation boundary.

code.finding: Unconditional `folderTree.set()` in `loadFolder` — the REQ-1 fix target; needs a sequenceNumber guard before this call so self-bootstrap never clobbers fresher in-memory state with a stale IPNS snapshot.
`ensureFolderLoaded` short-circuit — must be preserved intact when applying the REQ-1 guard to avoid re-regressing #498.
DFS child-check in `ensureFolderLoaded` — must also be preserved intact alongside the sequenceNumber guard.
`folder:updated` event definition — canonical model for the new `sharedFolder:updated` event required by REQ-3's sharedFolderTree projection.

Write-back logic that REQ-3 replaces: becomes an event-fed projection (listening to `sharedFolder:updated`) instead of direct state mutation; `withConflictRetry` dropped because CAS moves into the SDK client.
`encryptedIpnsKey` field — the direct analog for the new `item_name_encrypted bytea` column added by REQ-4; ECIES wrap/unwrap pattern mirrors this field exactly.
Migration to clone for REQ-4's `item_name_encrypted` column — additive structure (no data UPDATE), the correct zero-knowledge migration pattern.
ECIES wrap site for REQ-4 — itemName is encrypted here at share-creation time; also the invite flow entry point that must be included per user decision (A3).

workflow: Pre-merge e2e gate for fixes to e2e-detected regressions: dispatch `gh workflow run web-e2e.yml --ref <fix-branch>` immediately after push — direct dispatch resolves repo secrets without a `secrets: inherit` parent, faithfully reproducing the main-push run.

When a pending todo's premise depends on a PR 'proving out in staging/prod,' verify the PR's e2e status before treating that todo as unblocked — #9 was filed as gated on #498 proving out, but #498 was actively regressing main.

GSD pattern mapper (run before the planner) classifies all target files against existing analogs and verifies research line numbers against current source — catching stale references before planner consumes them.
Sequential executor execution (no worktree isolation) is safer than parallel worktrees for unattended AFK runs; reliability > speed when there is no human to recover from a parallel conflict.

When grouping todos, distinguish 'do together on one branch' (same through-line, complementary scope) from 'one supersedes the other' (the superseding work is long-horizon, so the superseded item must be resolved independently now).

friction: API stream idle timeout mid-response during the initial parallel fan-out research, requiring the user to redirect to a GSD phase instead of an ad-hoc research + plan.

GSD `branching_strategy: phase` silently created `feat/sdk-self-bootstrap-regression-fix-and-shared-folder-metadata` off HEAD during execute-phase init, potentially orphaning the 5 planning commits already on `feat/phase-48-...` — required explicit git log verification before spawning any executor.
1Password SSH signing requires keychain access and can hang during unattended execution — flagged as a potential wedge point for the AFK commit chain.
UAT steps (cold-reload verification, shared-write round-trip, itemName display) are not fully automatable via web-e2e alone — must be noted as partially unverified during AFK execution.
